name: Cloister at The Boca Raton
positioning: The original 1926 heart of The Boca Raton resort: Mediterranean-inspired architecture, secluded courtyards and tropical gardens, with newly redesigned rooms and a central spot near the resort's golf, racquet club and spa
best_for: Travelers who want historic, classically designed architecture at the center of the resort
Groups and families who want easy reach of the golf club, racquet club and spa
Guests traveling with a dog up to 35 pounds

facts.text: Cloister is the original heart of The Boca Raton and has welcomed guests since 1926.
The Boca Raton began in 1926 as an inn built by architect Addison Mizner.
Cloister is defined by Mediterranean-inspired architecture, secluded courtyards and lush tropical gardens.
Conde Nast Traveler calls Cloister the resort's most classically designed stay, with dark-wood furnishings and inconspicuous artwork.
The redesigned guestrooms honor the hotel's architectural character through a fresh, modern lens, with playful details.
Cloister's central location puts the resort's historic Golf Club, its Racquet Club and Spa Palmera within easy reach.
Cloister is the closest of the resort's stays to its main amenities, like dining and shopping.
Cloister guests have full resort access.
Cloister guests have access to the private amenities of The Boca Raton Club.
Cloister offers a fleet of bicycles.
Rooms have Molton Brown bath amenities.
Mizner Park, an outdoor district with a fine arts museum, shopping and dining, is about a five-minute drive north of the resort.

highlights.text: Cloister features rotating art collections and fashion collaborations throughout.
Cloister's rooms were newly redesigned in fall 2026.
Spa Palmera is an ode to the Alhambra Palace, with arches, stonework, mosaic tiles and a courtyard with a lap pool.
Two water taxis carry guests across Lake Boca Raton to the resort's private beachfront.

considerations.text: The resort's private beachfront is across Lake Boca Raton; water taxis carry guests there.
Dogs are welcome only up to 35 pounds.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
